name: personal_essay_vs_ai_tech_product
positive_pole: Introspective first-person Substack-style essays on self-acceptance, romance, ambition, and twentysomething life lessons.
negative_pole: Corporate/technical pages about AI infrastructure, LLMs, agent frameworks, and ML research products.
notes: The split is nearly categorical: emotional personal blogging vs. AI/ML company and research content.

name: ai_alignment_discourse_vs_web_design_craft
positive_pole: Long-form analytical writing about AI alignment, safety, misalignment risks, and the future of advanced AI systems, typically on rationalist/AI-research blogs.
negative_pole: Personal portfolios, web-design inspiration galleries, and creative-coding/indie-web showcases focused on visual craft and aesthetics rather than written argument.
notes: The split is nearly perfect: HIGH pages are essays from LessWrong, Anthropic, DeepMind, Cold Takes, etc., while LOW pages are designer portfolios and 'cool websites' directories.

name: startup_venture_capital_ness
positive_pole: Pages about founding startups, venture capital, accelerators, and Silicon Valley career paths for aspiring entrepreneurs.
negative_pole: Pages featuring literary poetry or technical machine-learning/interpretability content (neural network internals, transformers, attention).
notes: LOW pole mixes two distinct clusters (poetry and ML research), but both share being non-commercial/non-entrepreneurial intellectual or artistic content versus HIGH's uniformly startup/VC focus.

name: cultural_critique_vs_self_improvement
positive_pole: Long-form cultural, philosophical, geopolitical, or literary commentary on civilization, ideology, and the human condition (often citing theorists, novels, or historical events).
negative_pole: Practical first-person advice posts on personal productivity, learning, research methodology, and how to do great work as an individual.
notes: HIGH pieces are external/world-facing essays and reference works (Baudrillard, Yeats, Fukuyama, war crimes reporting); LOW pieces are 'how I work / how to learn / how to do research' self-help for knowledge workers.

name: quantitative_business_analysis_vs_ai_creativity_reflection
positive_pole: Pages presenting quantitative, formula-driven analyses of business, finance, startups, or computer-science algorithms with concrete metrics, math, and how-to mechanics.
negative_pole: Personal landing pages and reflective essays by AI/HCI researchers and artists musing on creativity, human-AI interaction, and the philosophy of AI tools.
notes: HIGH cluster is technical/quantitative (SaaS metrics, VC math, algorithms, probability distributions); LOW cluster is personal-bio pages and qualitative essays about AI, creativity, and design.

name: intellectual_self_improvement_vs_relational_emotional
positive_pole: Long-form essays and book recommendations on how to think, learn, do research, and solve hard problems—aimed at cultivating the reader's intellectual craft.
negative_pole: Personal/cultural writing about relationships, dating, loneliness, and AI companions, or product pages about AI tools—focused on emotional life and contemporary tech culture rather than intellectual self-cultivation.
notes: HIGH cluster is dominated by Paul Graham / Hamming / Tao style essays on thinking and research; LOW cluster is dominated by Substack-style essays on romance, friendship, AI companionship, plus a few AI product/landing pages.

name: personal_bio_vs_tech_essay
positive_pole: Personal homepage/about-me pages or biographical profiles of individuals (typically young AI/tech researchers and founders) listing their education, jobs, and interests.
negative_pole: Topical long-form essays and opinion pieces about software, web design, interfaces, or internet culture, written as arguments rather than self-introductions.
notes: HIGH set is overwhelmingly first-person 'about me' pages plus a couple of biographical profiles/interviews; LOW set is essays arguing a thesis about tech/web/UX.

name: relationships_and_social_connection_focus
positive_pole: The page is an essay or guide centered on interpersonal connection—how to meet, befriend, converse with, or build community/trust with other people.
negative_pole: The page is a personal essay about work, productivity, time, or life trajectory, with the individual's relationship to their own work/time as the central topic rather than relationships with others.
notes: Both clusters are reflective personal-essay blog posts; the distinguishing axis is subject matter (social/relational vs. work/time/self).

name: commentary_vs_frontier_tech
positive_pole: Personal blog-style commentary, criticism, and meta-discussion about the internet, AI discourse, and online culture (often opinionated essays reacting to other writing).
negative_pole: Institutional or company-style announcements describing ambitious frontier science/engineering projects (biotech, energy, hardware, neuroscience, moonshots) and their technical missions.
notes: HIGH pages are written in first person reflecting on media/AI/discourse; LOW pages are landing pages or press releases pitching deep-tech R&D.

name: design_taste_and_craft_discourse
positive_pole: Essays and studio/product pages centered on aesthetic taste, craft, and the artistry of design (visual, product, or brand-making) as the core subject.
negative_pole: Utilitarian posts about personal-productivity systems, note-taking, second-brain tools, knowledge management, and lists of tools/tips for organizing information.
notes: Both clusters are tech-adjacent and often blog-style; the discriminating axis is aesthetic/craft/taste discourse vs. productivity/PKM/tooling discourse.
